basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A spatial unit of land with identity and boundary, not the title or rights over it.
Geometry is tied to a declared coordinate reference system and survey evidence.
Subdivision and merger create new parcels with lineage, rather than editing the old ones.
Differs from address, building and site, which are separate records.

may: Read parcel geometry, area and identifiers from the authoritative cadastre.
Report discrepancies between survey evidence and recorded boundaries.
Compute area with the CRS and method stated.
mustNot: Treat a parcel record as proof of ownership.
Treat digitized map lines as surveyed boundaries.
Enter private land without permission during inspections.

considerations: Land records decide who can live on and use land; errors can dispossess people.
Customary and informal tenure is often missing from cadastres.
Combined parcel and owner data can enable profiling of individuals.

items: Area in square metres or hectares, computed in a declared CRS or on the ellipsoid.
Boundary vertex coordinates with positional accuracy in metres.
Elevation in metres above a stated vertical datum.
A parcel is recognised by its parcel identifier, boundary markers, fences and survey plans.
It is confused with the ownership title, the postal address and adjoining parcels.
EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset for CRS codes.
